block.text: Recommendation. Round 15 correctly retires the historical effort allocation as a funding rule. My independent ranking of the 34 current priority/reserve candidates begins topical APR-246 → RM4404 → BLU-3797 → NDC-9009 → mIGF-Gel → exact 8015-P2 → AAT for donor-lung preservation/perfusion. These are small, conditional investments that could create or eliminate a commercial option. BLU ranks third; this is not a recommendation to fund seven complete programs.

The objective is discounted financial value retained by ddiscov, after subsequent development costs, commercial costs, license payments, royalties, partner sharing and financing dilution. Patient benefit matters because it supports adoption and reimbursement, but valuable patient care and a valuable owned business are different outputs. This objective is an explicit assumption; a philanthropic health-value ranking would favor several inexpensive repurposed treatments more strongly.

For an action a, the relevant comparison is: expected value of the best decision after learning from a, minus the value of the best decision available now, minus the cost of a. Divide that increment by the action’s cost only when comparing similarly bounded opportunities. Counting a hypothetical whole-drug NPV against a tiny literature-review bill would manufacture an enormous, meaningless return.

I start with the substantial attrition and financing burden of drug development, then update for exact-article functional evidence, clinically relevant tissue exposure, replication, feasible delivery and a defensible commercial position. Selected cases, biomarkers, related molecules and favorable animal models each update different uncertainties. They cannot be multiplied as if they were independent successes. A proposed future positive result is not evidence already earned.

The public record does not identify license prices, net revenue, eligible reachable patients, clinical development budgets or retained ownership well enough to support credible numerical EV/$ estimates. The ranking is therefore ordinal and conditional. The cost ranges below are analyst planning judgments, not quotations, commitments, full program budgets or estimates of approval probability.

All development tranches are hypothetical and unexecuted. Rights, licensing, GLP toxicology, GMP clinical manufacture, trials and commercialization are excluded. Requiring new platforms or inaccessible materials can exceed these ranges. Time to a decision is not time to revenue. The ranges overlap and do not by themselves establish the ordering.

The mechanistic case includes active/inactive protein and recipient protease comparisons in murine cold preservation and transplantation. That is more causally informative than an isolated biomarker result. It does not establish that a warm-perfusion product produces durable transplant benefit. <link href="https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6078707/" color="#176289">Primary transplant study</link>.

A processing intervention could create value through more usable grafts or better graft function. Initial qualification is bounded; organs, integration and clinical adoption are expensive later. Measure active protease inhibition, not protein mass alone. A differentiated process, formulation or contract must give ddiscov a share beyond established protein suppliers and perfusion operators.

The most robust judgments are to keep the legacy majority allocation retired, preserve the local challengers, account for incumbent value capture, and stop repetitive closed audits. The exact APR/RM/BLU order has only moderate-to-low confidence: a favorable BLU license or an expensive ocular formulation can reverse it. mIGF versus NDC/P2 is also close. Numerical ranks here are work priorities under stated assumptions, not measured differences in expected dollars.

original_claim_scope: Initial formulation, active potency and process qualification before scarce organs; value depends on enabling a useful later graft-function/utilization decision and a differentiated process, formulation or contracted contribution.
inherited_interpretation: Qualification is explicitly the original AAT priced tranche. Do not import the P2 human-function envelope or invalidate AAT rank merely because the first step is qualification. The illustrative $30–100k/two-to-four-month envelope excludes scarce organs and transplant validation, plus original general rights/licensing/GLP/GMP/trial/commercialization exclusions. Compare actual information yield, feasibility, remaining costs and retained value. A narrower irrelevant assay or substantial cost expansion still requires a new comparison.
